name: CA-30
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The district's 21-point Democratic lean, Friedman's lopsided fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 96% all point to a comfortable incumbent hold; with no polls or expert ratings available, structural fundamentals carry the forecast.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Friedman or an unforeseen scandal could narrow the race, though nothing in the current evidence points that way.

overview:
California's 30th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the party. Laura Friedman, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election and faces Republican Scott Meyers, a challenger with minimal financial backing. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing.

Friedman has raised about $995,000 and holds roughly $520,000 on hand, while Meyers has raised about $123,000 with only around $5,000 available. No outside groups have engaged on either side, and prediction markets put Democratic chances near 96%. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, an established incumbent, and a vast resource gap makes this seat a strong Democratic hold, with the Republican challenger facing steep structural odds in November.
